glosses: to worry, to be anxious, to trouble
passive of забо́тить (zabótitʹ)
проявлять заботу, беспокойство о ком-либо или о чём-либо, ухаживать за кем-либо, окружать кого-что-нибудь заботами, попечением

examples.text: Он много заботился о своём здоровье.
Вам ни о чем не нужно заботиться — всё будет в порядке.
Она заботилась о чужих детях, как о родных.

glosses: проявлять беспокойство, волноваться о чём-либо, прилагать старание к чему-нибудь

examples.text: Я пишу, как подсказывает память, не заботясь о последовательности, о хронологии.

glosses: To follow with the eyes; to look in the direction of (someone or something departing).

examples.text: The marshes were just a long black horizontal line then, as I stopped to look after him; and the river was just another horizontal line, not nearly so broad nor yet so black; and the sky was just a row of long angry red lines and dense black lines intermixed.

glosses: To seek out, to look for.

examples.text: My subject does not necessarily oblige me to look after this water, or point forth the place whereunto 'tis now retreated.
I have sent my intended husband to look after my lover […].
If they are not married, they should be looking after a wife.
Sliding through the world: that is how, in a bygone age, they used to designate lives like his: looking after his interests, quietly prospering, attracting no attention.

glosses: To care for; to keep safe.

examples.text: He asked me to look after his daughter while he was away.
The station is clearly well looked after, making it a worthy gateway to the resort.

"And I thought: if muggins here, a 37-year-old government minister who can look after myself, feels that way, then we need to really think about how we're putting in place a level of protection for women.

glosses: To have as one's business; to manage, be responsible for.
To expect, look forward to.

examples.text: Mens hearts failing them for feare, and for looking after those things which are comming on the earth; For the powers of heauen shall be shaken.

glosses: To look after, to care for.

examples.text: My elderly mother needs to be taken care of.

glosses: To deal with, handle.

examples.text: Can somebody take care of the customers while I clean this mess?

People had time to think up some questions, including reporters who shouted “Are you going to shoot down the balloon?” at President Biden shortly before the dirigible came down. “We’re going to take care of it,” the president told reporters in Syracuse, N.Y., where he was visiting family.

glosses: To kill.

examples.text: In the motion picture ‘The Godfather’, gangster Virgil Sollozzo took care of Luca Brasi by having him strangled.

glosses: Proteger algo o a alguien del daño o el desgaste.
Aplicar atención y esmero a una acción.
Aplicar la inteligencia a la consideración detenida o sistemática de un asunto.
To be troubled; to give way to mental anxiety or doubt.

examples.text: So you go along for a long time / And nothing seems to worry your mind / But what it adds up to / It's the side effect / That finally gets to you

glosses: Disturb the peace of mind of; afflict with mental agitation or distress; to exercise.

examples.text: Your tone of voice worries me.
That worries the government, which fears that environmental activism could become the foundation for more general political opposition.

glosses: To harass; to irritate or distress.

examples.text: The President was worried into military action by persistent advisors.

glosses: To seize or shake by the throat, especially of a dog or wolf.

examples.text: Your dog’s been worrying sheep again.
This is the Dog, that worried the Cat, that killed the Rat, that ate the Malt, that lay in the Houſe that Jack built.

glosses: To touch repeatedly; to fiddle with.

examples.text: Christian paced the caravan, worrying his beard.
So what if I wanted to touch my nose to the windshield? Who was it hurting? Why was it that he could repeatedly worry his change and bite his lower lip without the threat of punishment?
No stories, no arguments. He just worries his prayer beads.

glosses: To strangle.

examples.text: We read (Law's Memor. Pref. lix.) that "one John Brugh, a notorious warlock (wizard) in the parochin of Fossoquhy, by the space of thirty-six years, was worried at a stake and burned, 1643."

glosses: A strong feeling of anxiety.

examples.text: I'm afflicted by worry throughout the night.
"Worry never solved any problems. Only gives you ulcers."

glosses: An instance or cause of such a feeling.

examples.text: My main worry is that I'll miss the train.

glosses: A person who causes worry.

examples.text: They could never make him speak a word, although he was old enough, in short, he was a perfect worry night and day.
